description: The exact CPV code set for banking & payments in Slovenian practice is not yet fixed. Confirmed anchors so far: 66110000 bančne storitve, 66510000 zavarovalniške storitve, division 66 generally. Codes for POS/ATM hardware, card personalisation, payment gateways and cash-in-transit are not yet enumerated.

Evidencna naročila (below-threshold, record-only procurements) and utilities-sector procurement under ZJNPOV/infrastructure rules are largely invisible in the notice stream, yet a lot of POS/ATM and cash-handling spend sits there.

The key Slovenian public buyers of banking/payments services — Banka Slovenije, Ministrstvo za finance / Uprava RS za javna plačila (UJP), FURS, Pošta Slovenije, SDH-owned entities, larger municipalities — have not been mapped to their portal buyer identifiers in this pass.

ZJN-3 requires publication of 'obvestilo o spremembi pogodbe med njeno veljavnostjo' (contract-modification notices), which is where extensions and value increases on multi-year banking contracts appear. No dedicated capture route was identified.
Uradni list RS is running training on a 'prenova Portala javnih naročil' with new e-forms — a schema migration of the primary source is in progress or imminent.
Almost nothing in this cell exists in English apart from TED and a gov.si institutional page; English-only monitoring would miss essentially all below-threshold and national-level notices.

By construction this cell only sees contracts above the EU publication thresholds. Slovenian banking/payments contracts below threshold — likely the majority by count, e.g. single-branch ATM servicing, small card-personalisation or POS lots — never reach TED.

Commercial banks in Slovenia (NLB, NKBM, SKB, Intesa Sanpaolo Bank, Addiko, Gorenjska banka) and shared infrastructure operators such as Bankart are mostly private entities and are generally not contracting authorities, so their vendor selections do not appear on TED at all. TED captures them mainly as suppliers/winners, not buyers.

CPV coding is chosen by the buyer and is frequently imprecise: payments-adjacent work is often filed under IT services (72xxxxxx), office/financial machinery (30144200 versus 30123000-family), or generic financial services (66000000), so a strict four-code filter will under-recall.
TED spans two generations of data: legacy TED-schema XML for older notices and eForms (UBL 2.3) for recent ones, with different field structures and value semantics.

TED's non-Slovenian language versions of SI notices are largely machine-translated summaries; the substantive tender documentation stays in Slovenian on the national portal and is not carried into TED.

EU-funded programme data on the Funding & Tenders Portal (projects with Slovenian banking, fintech or public-payments beneficiaries) was identified but not systematically explored in this pass, and no confirmed Slovenian payments project was located.

TED (Tenders Electronic Daily) was not systematically probed in this pass as a route to Slovenian EU-co-financed award notices above threshold. TED carries structured award data including winning-vendor names and is the natural EU-level complement to enarocanje.si.

Audit and control bodies were not covered: Računsko sodišče RS (Court of Audit), the Urad RS za nadzor proračuna / AFCOS function, and the European Court of Auditors. Their reports name specific EU-financed IT projects, contract values and irregularities - an independent evidence channel on donor-financed procurement outcomes.

Several candidate landing pages were inferred from search-result context rather than fetched: the URSOO NOO page on gov.si, the SPIRIT razpisi index, the MDP razpisi listing, and the EIB projects search endpoint. Their exact current URLs may differ.

IFC (World Bank Group private-sector arm) and the Council of Europe Development Bank were not searched, and the EIB Group's own corporate procurement/consultancy notice board was noted only indirectly. Each can finance or advise Slovenian financial institutions.

The Slovenian glossary built here covers funding and procurement vocabulary (javni razpis, javni poziv, javno naročilo, obvestilo o oddaji naročila, NOO, EKP, ESRR, kohezijski sklad, finančni posrednik, Sklad skladov, sofinanciranje, operacija, upravičenec) but is thin on payments-specific Slovenian technical terms in a procurement context (e.g. plačilni sistem, kartično poslovanje, bankomat, POS terminal, jedrni bančni sistem).

Only Informator javnih razpisov (and possibly Mercell/TendersInfo) claim private-sector tender coverage for SI. Private RFPs from SI banks, which are outside the public-procurement regime unless the buyer is state-owned, are largely invisible in every source found.

TED only carries above-threshold notices. Below-threshold SI procurement (evidencna narocila, narocila male vrednosti) exists mainly on the national portal and in a few SI commercial services; archive retention for these is unclear.

For every commercial reseller (TendersInfo, GlobalTenders, TenderImpulse, BidDetail, TendersTech, javnirazpisi.com), how far back the SI archive reaches and whether historical award notices are exportable was not established - only teaser pages were reachable.

No SI-localised mapping was built of the CPV codes that matter for banking and payments (e.g. banking services 66110000-range, ATM/payment terminal hardware 30123000-range, financial IT services 72xxxxxx). Aggregator taxonomies use their own branch labels rather than CPV.

Slovenian searching covered javna narocila, javni razpisi, javna nabava, obvescanje, bonitete, odprti podatki. Not yet exercised: 'obvestilo o oddaji narocila' (award notice), 'evidencno narocilo', 'okvirni sporazum' (framework agreement), 'narocila male vrednosti', and Uradni list RS archive terminology.
Investigative non-profit media (Necenzurirano.si, Pod črto, Oštro.si) not confirmed in this run despite being the archetype for FOI-based contract revelations.
English-language Slovene business coverage (STA English, Slovenia Times, Total Slovenia News) not enumerated; the cell is sl-weighted by design but en cross-checks aid triage.
No Slovene press-clipping/aggregation service identified (e.g. Kliping, Press Clipping d.o.o.) that would give licensed full-text across paywalled outlets in one feed.
Archive depth of the paywalled dailies (how far back site search reaches, and whether old.delo.si-style legacy archives exist for Finance/Dnevnik/Večer) is unknown.
Vendor-side actor map is thin: only Bankart surfaced explicitly; no confirmation of press coverage naming international processors/ATM vendors in Slovenia.

Careers pages were mapped only for NLB, SID banka and Deželna banka. Other significant SI banks/PSPs (NKBM/OTP banka, SKB, Addiko, Sparkasse, Gorenjska banka, Delavska hranilnica, Intesa Sanpaolo Bank, plus Bankart and Halcom as employers) have no first-party hiring feed recorded.

Award and recognition programmes are unmapped (see negative finding). Candidates to check: Slovensko društvo INFORMATIKA project awards, Zlata nit / Top Employer, Diamanti slovenskega gospodarstva, Netokracija/tech-media awards.

Job boards do not expose their listings to general web search, so no source in this slice has a proven machine-readable feed. No RSS/API endpoint was confirmed for MojeDelo, Optius, Zaposlitev.si or ESS.

Vendor-side coverage rests on Halcom and Bankart. International vendors likely active in Slovenia (Temenos, Diebold Nixdorf, Nexi, Worldline, Comtrade, Marand, Iskratel/S&T, Printec) have no press/reference feed recorded in this cell.
Job postings expire and are deleted; conference programmes are replaced per edition. Without snapshotting, this cell's evidence base decays within weeks.

Local-language coverage was achieved for job ads, conferences and trade media, but no established Slovenian term was found for 'weak-signal award announcement'; English vendor terminology (core banking, instant payments, migration) dominates job-ad titles even in Slovenian postings.

Below-threshold 'evidenčna naročila' are not published as notices; only aggregate statistics and a >10,000 EUR annual listing duty exist. Many banking/payments purchases (software modules, terminal maintenance, card supplies) plausibly sit under the threshold.
The structure and rate limits of the enarocanje.si /arhiv/{id}/ archive and of the IPRS decisions index (opaque hash slugs) were not established in this pass.
No CPV code list for banking/payments/terminal procurement was assembled in this cell.
The separate regime for utilities/infrastructure buyers (ZJN-3 'infrastrukturno področje') and for the ZJNPOV defence/security act was noted only in passing.
English-language coverage of Slovenian procurement rules is thin outside TED; national notices are published in Slovenian only.
The banking/payments subset of DKOM decisions has not been enumerated — only the corpus containers were mapped.

Sector regulators and specialised oversight bodies adjacent to this cell were not searched in this pass: Banka Slovenije (as supervisor and as a contracting authority), AJPES, Urad RS za preprečevanje pranja denarja, and the Fiskalni svet.
No freedom-of-information (ZDIJZ) route was assessed for material these bodies hold but do not publish — e.g. full bid documentation referenced in a DKOM decision.

Investigative media and civil-society watchdogs that translate DKOM/KPK/Court of Audit output into narrative (e.g. Oštro, Pod črto, Transparency International Slovenia, Necenzurirano) were not covered in this pass.
No verified crosswalk was established between DKOM decision numbers (018-nnn/YYYY), eNaročanje publication numbers (JN.../NMV...), TED notice IDs and ERAR supplier tax IDs.
Liveness, robots.txt policy, rate limits and terms of use were not checked for any domain in this slice — per instructions, URL verification is a separate deterministic pass.
It is unknown whether the UJP-sourced executed-payment data published on enarocanje.si is available in bulk/machine-readable form, or only per-contract in HTML.
ERAR's underlying JSON/XHR endpoints were not probed, so the practical collection method for vendor-level payment data remains undetermined.
No CPV code list for banking/payments/ATM/card-personalisation/core-banking services was assembled, so none of the procurement datasets can yet be filtered down to the sector of interest.
Banka Slovenije's own procurement publications, and those of state-owned banks (NLB, SID banka) as contracting entities, were not covered in this cell.
EU-level publication (TED / eForms) of Slovenian above-threshold notices was not covered here, and OCDS endpoint URLs for Slovenia were identified only indirectly via the OCP registry.
Reuse licences are inconsistent across the relevant datasets: ERAR is CC BY 4.0, but the contracts dataset shows 'ni določena' and AJPES bulk products are priced.
The e-invoice dataset (zbirka e-računov) parent page was not fetched; its resource granularity, licence and whether supplier names are exposed are unknown.
Exact procurement URLs for Banka Slovenije and for ZZZS's corporate (non-provider) section remain unknown.

No CPV-code-driven query set was built this run; without it, payment/ATM/card/IT procurement cannot be separated from the very large volume of unrelated tenders these buyers issue (medical devices, mail transport, real estate).

Naročnik filtering fails silently unless exact registered legal names and aliases are known (SID banka d.d.; Kapitalska družba d.d.; Zavod za zdravstveno zavarovanje Slovenije; Zavod za pokojninsko in invalidsko zavarovanje Slovenije; Pošta Slovenije d.o.o.; Banka Slovenije; Ministrstvo za finance — Finančna uprava RS; Slovenski državni holding d.d.).

Naročila male vrednosti and non-binding 'javni pozivi za zbiranje informativnih ponudb' (notably at Pošta Slovenije and ZPIZ) sit below national-portal visibility or outside it entirely, yet they are the earliest demand signals.
Award notices (obvestilo o oddaji naročila) and realised spend (ERAR/OPSI) were identified as sources but no join key between them was established.
Both primary portals (enarocanje.si SPA with a hash-fragment router, ejn.gov.si JSF/XHTML with viewstate) resist naive HTTP scraping, and no robots.txt / ToS review was performed this run.

Slovenian coverage was strong; English coverage is structurally thin because Slovenian notices are published in Slovenian only, with English available mainly as TED summaries of above-threshold notices.

Only 5 mestne obcine (Ljubljana, Maribor, Celje, Kranj, Koper) plus Novo mesto and Skofja Loka were reached. Slovenia has 212 obcine including 12 mestne obcine; Nova Gorica, Ptuj, Murska Sobota, Velenje, Slovenj Gradec, Krsko and Domzale were not covered.

Municipal utilities beyond transport and parking were not investigated: water/waste (VOKA Snaga, Komunala), energy (Energetika Ljubljana), sports and culture javni zavodi, and municipal libraries - all of which take counter and kiosk payments and issue cards.

No notice-level search interface or API for enarocanje.si was located; it is unclear whether structured/eForms exports exist for below-EU-threshold Slovene notices, which is precisely the band where municipal payments purchases live.

The glossary for acquiring-side vocabulary in Slovene municipal procurement was only partially built. Terms confirmed in use: plačilni terminal, POS, kartični sistem, brezstična kartica, čitalnik vozovnic, parkomat, urbanomat, evidenčno naročilo, letni seznam oddanih javnih naročil, Valú. Not yet validated: 'pridobivanje kartičnih plačil', 'sprejemanje plačilnih kartic', 'kartično poslovanje', 'gotovinsko poslovanje', 'blagajniško poslovanje', 'e-vozovnica', 'validator', 'account-based ticketing' in Slovene usage.
Italian and Hungarian bilingual municipalities were not covered in their minority languages. Koper/Capodistria, Izola/Isola, Piran/Pirano publish in Italian, and Lendava/Lendva in Hungarian.
No historical/archival dimension was established. Only Kranj was confirmed to publish a procurement archive; the retention policy of enarocanje.si notices and of DKOM decisions was not checked.

Intesa Sanpaolo Bank Slovenija's own site (intesasanpaolobank.si) was not directly crawled for a local 'dobavitelji / portal dobaviteljev' page, even though sibling subsidiaries in Serbia and Albania publish exactly such a page.

Bank career/RFI announcements, LinkedIn posts and vendor press releases — the practical 'reveals-indirectly' channel where Slovenian bank sourcing becomes visible (who won an IT/payments contract) — were not scouted in this pass.
Annual reports / sustainability (ESG, CSRD) reports of each bank were not mined; these routinely disclose supplier counts, local-supplier share, supplier ESG screening and outsourcing arrangements.

Regulatory outsourcing registers: EBA outsourcing-guidelines registers and DORA ICT third-party registers are maintained by each bank and reported to Banka Slovenije, but no route to any published extract was explored.

Parent-group sourcing channels for Addiko (Vienna), Gorenjska banka (AIK, Belgrade) and OTP (Budapest) would require German, Serbian and Hungarian search terms; only sl/en/limited de-it were used in this pass.
Bank-owned shared infrastructure beyond Bankart (e.g. Bankart's own supplier onboarding, and any bank-consortium procurement vehicles) was only hypothesised, not confirmed.

Direct newsroom/reference-page crawls were not performed for comtrade.com / comtradedigital.com, marand.si, payten.com (SI locale), and dieboldnixdorf.com newsroom; their exact URLs are inferred rather than observed.

Vendors and integrators plausibly serving Slovenian banks were not searched in this pass: SRC d.o.o., Unistar LC, Kontron/S&T Slovenija, RRC, NIL, Result, Špica, Iskratel/Iskra, Gemalto/Thales (card personalisation), Giesecke+Devrient, Sopra Banking, Finastra, Backbase, BSS/ProCredit-type niche vendors, plus Mastercard/Visa Slovenia programme announcements.

Searches were vendor-led and skewed toward NLB and Nova KBM. Little coverage of SKB (OTP), Gorenjska banka (AIK), Addiko, Sparkasse, Delavska hranilnica, Deželna banka Slovenije, LON, Primorska hranilnica Vipava, Pošta Slovenije, and the savings banks (hranilnice), which have different and often smaller vendors.

LinkedIn company pages and vendor career/job postings — often the earliest and most granular signal of a specific bank project — were not searched; nor were conference/event agendas (Halcom events, Bankart forums, Dnevi slovenske informatike, Bančni vestnik) where implementations are presented jointly by bank and vendor.
No Croatian/Serbian-language searching was done, although ASEE, Payten, Comtrade and Halcom communicate regional wins primarily in hr/sr and Slovenian subsidiaries are frequently mentioned there.

Non-bank acquirers and PSPs operating in Slovenia (e.g. domestic Activa card system, foreign acquirers, e-money institutions notified to Banka Slovenije) were not individually enumerated in this pass.
The procurement portal's filter syntax was observed but the payments-relevant CPV code set was not yet enumerated or validated against live results.

No archival source was established for notices that expire or are withdrawn from the portal, and no vendor-side reference/case-study channel (NCR/Atos/Worldline/Thales/IDEMIA/Diebold Slovenia references) was scouted.

It was not established whether Bankart or the commercial banks fall under the Slovenian public-procurement act as utility/sectoral contracting entities, which determines whether any of their buying must be published at all.

Local-language coverage was achieved for procurement, Flik, ATM and personalisation terms, but no Slovene terminology was located for tokenisation, HSM/key management or scheme certification procurement.

The specific PISP/AISP (storitev odreditve plačil / storitev informiranja o računih) register listing was not isolated to a single stable URL; it appears to live under the supervised-entities register search rather than on its own page.

Insurance-sector registers (AZN – Agencija za zavarovalni nadzor) and the insurance association (Slovensko zavarovalno združenje) were not searched in this run; insurers are significant procurers of payment/IT technology.

Payment-infrastructure operators (Bankart d.o.o. as card/processing operator, Bankart/BS scheme participant lists, SEPA scheme adherence lists) were seen only as NSP attendees; their participant/member lists were not harvested.

Slovene-language searching was performed for every category in this cell, but no Italian/Hungarian minority-language or Croatian-language variants were attempted, and English coverage was limited to EU-level registers.

No register of qualified/registered suppliers (bidders) for Slovenian public procurement was identified; e-JN appears to expose contracting authorities and notices but not a public supplier directory.
